prompt: packages/japanese/prompts/reading-validator.md, adapted to the two-document shape: classify each option A-only / B-only / both / neither against 文章1 and 文章2, then apply the stem, counting paraphrase (hypernym-for-hyponym, 協力/協働-style pairs) as a hit.

note: Round A, pass B over the same 12 authored rows (verdicts tougou-B.md). 12 PASS, 0 AMBIGUOUS, picks equal to the shipped key on every row (12/12 across both passes). One caveat it raised and this record keeps rather than buries: the four 相違 rows lean on the authoring convention, because 「内容が一致しないものはどれか」 can also be read as 'which statement contradicts the documents', and under that alternative reading their three verbatim single-document quotes would all be consistent with one document and no option would match. Both passes keyed the rows the same way under the relation-naming reading, and the real 大問11 小問 does ask the reader to hold both texts at once, but the stem's second meaning is a live risk for those four rows and belongs to whoever revisits this block. Correlated-error limit, recorded rather than hidden: both passes ran on the author model's own family, so their agreement is not independence. What the pairing tests is whether a reader who cannot see the key lands on exactly one option under two different procedures, not whether a second model would agree.

Repairs here: 海図が書き換わった→書き換えられた and 小河川の大返し→折り返し (in the passage and in the evidence span that quotes it), the dangling 市は…支えられない given its predicate and ままなら→ままでは (which also moves the option that lifts the sentence verbatim, so the lift stays a lift), 縮小が打つのは→削るのは (again mirrored into the evidence), 肥育は立った→上がった, 事実が論の裏に置いてある→置かれている.
